evidence_locator.observation: Cycle count is the evolution coordinate. Explicit accumulation uses a recorded strain cycle, with optional control-cycle updates; direct measurement and separate dynamic calculation are alternative amplitude sources. Explicit here distinguishes the cycle-package strategy from cycle-by-cycle modelling, not the time integrator.

Accumulation combines direction, amplitude, cyclic history, stress, void ratio and polarization factors. The source restricts its amplitude law near yield-surface encounters and discusses direct residual extrapolation instead. History depends on past amplitudes, not just a raw cycle counter.

Tensorial amplitude and back-polarization extend the law beyond scalar axial amplitude. A polarization-change DSS experiment is used to determine the two polarization constants. Initialization alternatives are supplied; component constraints and dimensions still need equation review.

Multiple-source amplitude superposition and frequency correction are explicitly approximate. Implementation separates implicit, recording and pseudo-creep modes and references a companion intergranular-strain hypoplastic law.

The centrifuge example uses additional accumulation calibration and adjusts selected companion constants to the second cycle. The settlement comparison therefore cannot be labelled a prediction made without specimen-specific response information.

Source supplies conventions, a Matsuoka–Nakai admissibility criterion, a settlement-formula consistency argument, and references needed for companion-law and lineage tracing. These do not resolve the exact journal variant.
